newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arabs condemn intervention in Iraq by neighbours.
newsitem.headline: Arabs condemn intervention in Iraq by neighbours.

text.p: Arab foreign ministers condemned on Saturday Turkish, Iranian or any other intervention in northern Iraq and said a proposed Turkish buffer zone there would be a violation of Iraqi territory.

An Arab League statement said the ministers, at a meeting in Cairo, described the situation in northern Iraq as serious as a result of what it called "Turkish violations on the pretext of setting up a so-called security belt or danger zone".

"The Council (of ministers) expressed its extreme concern at developments in the situation as a result of regional interventions which threaten the unity, security and safety of the territory of the Iraqi republic," it said. "The Council
strongly condemns the intervention by some neighbouring countries in the internal affairs of the territory of an Arab League member state," it added.
The statement mentioned Turkey by name but not Iran, which Iraq says has supported the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan against the Baghdad-backed Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP).
It also did not mention the United States, which has attacked Iraqi targets in retaliation for Baghdad's support for the KDP offensive into the town of Arbil last month.
The Arab ministers said they supported Iraqi independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity.
They also called for early implementaton of Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the United Nations as a means to spare the Iraqi people any further suffering from U.N. sanctions.
